name: Sale, standard rate 5 %
description: The general rate on a taxable supply of goods or services made in Bhutan
legal_reference: Goods and Services Tax Act of Bhutan 2020 (consolidated with the amendments of 2021, 2022 and 2025), s. 12 — GST applies to taxable supplies and taxable imports; s. 14(1) — the supplier is liable on a taxable supply made within Bhutan; s. 16 and s. 25 — the tax is the rate of Schedule I applied to the value of the supply; Schedule I, paragraph 1 — "Other than the zero rate prescribed in Schedule V, the applicable GST rate on taxable supplies and taxable imports of goods and services shall be 5%" (amended by the GST (Amendment) Act of Bhutan 2025); s. 2 — the Act is in force from 1 January 2026 and does not apply retroactively. Every supply that is neither exempt (Schedule IV) nor zero-rated (Schedule V) is standard-rated.

name: Sale, zero-rated (export)
description: Goods declared for export and exported, services supplied to a customer outside Bhutan, international transport (Schedule V)
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 28 — GST applies at zero per cent to a zero-rated supply; Schedule V, paragraph 2 — a sale of goods declared for export under the Customs Act of Bhutan 2017 and exported (or sold by a licensed duty-free vendor to a tourist on proof of exit); paragraph 9 — services supplied to a customer outside Bhutan who uses or enjoys them outside Bhutan; paragraph 12 — international transport and related services. A zero-rated supply is a taxable supply: s. 29 keeps the input tax credit for the purpose of making it.

name: Sale, exempt
description: A supply Schedule IV exempts: residential lease, financial services, education, health, rice, edible oil, salt
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 26 — GST does not apply to an exempt supply listed in Schedule IV; s. 27 — the supplier has no input tax credit to the extent an acquisition is for making an exempt supply. Schedule IV, A: paragraph 2 (right to occupy and reside in residential premises), paragraph 3 (sale of residential premises, except the first sale of a newly built one), paragraph 5 (financial services, except a specific fee), paragraph 10 (education services), paragraph 11 (health services); Schedule IV, C: rice, edible oils of the listed headings, salt, carriages for disabled persons, sanitary towels and nappies, by Bhutan Trade Classification code.

name: Purchase, standard rate 5 %
description: A taxable purchase at the standard rate whose input tax is deducted
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 32 and following — a taxable person is allowed a credit for the input tax incurred on an acquisition made for the purpose of its taxable supplies; s. 44 — the net amount of the return is the output tax less the allowable input tax credits; Schedule I, paragraph 1 — 5 %. Deducted in full when the purchase serves taxable or zero-rated supplies only; s. 36 and s. 37 apportion the credit when it also serves exempt supplies, which this code does not do.

name: Purchase, standard rate 5 %, input tax not deductible
description: A purchase whose input tax the Act blocks — entertainment, club memberships, passenger vehicles and what is used with them
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 34 — no input tax credit for an acquisition used to provide entertainment (unless entertainment is the person's economic activity), for a membership of a sporting, social or recreational club, for a lottery supply, for the acquisition or import of a passenger vehicle, or for goods or services used directly in connection with one. The tax charged by the supplier follows the expense to account 6530 and reaches no box.

name: Purchase, exempt
description: An exempt supply bought for the business
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 26 and Schedule IV — an exempt supply bought for the business (financial services, residential lease, education, health and the listed goods): no GST is charged and no input tax arises; the return has no row for an exempt purchase.

name: Import of goods, GST paid at customs clearance
description: GST charged on a taxable import, paid at customs clearance and claimed as input tax
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 12 and s. 14(2) — GST applies to a taxable import and the importer is liable; s. 47 — the GST on a taxable import is paid at customs clearance under the Customs Act of Bhutan 2017; s. 32 — the importer deducts it as input tax in its return. Posted to 2125 (import GST payable at the border) until the customs payment is matched.

name: Imported B2B service, reverse-charged and deductible
description: A service supplied by a person outside Bhutan to a business customer in Bhutan, taxed to the recipient who may deduct the tax
legal_reference: GST Act of Bhutan 2020, s. 14(3) — the purchaser is liable for GST on a taxable supply of imported business-to-business services; s. 33 — the customer is treated as incurring both output tax and input tax and is allowed the input tax credit provided it has accounted for the output tax; s. 18 — the value of the imported B2B service. The output tax is declared in box 1R and the credit in box 2R, so the net effect for a fully taxable customer is nil.
